/-- PROBE 2 (the CONVERSE): `hlift` itself, plus bare existence of an effective degree-`g`
divisor over each residue field, reconstructs `pt`, `hsq` AND `heff`.  Together with
`exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible` this makes the "reduction" an EQUIVALENCE:
the square carries no content beyond `hlift`. -/
theorem probe_converse_tautology {J : Scheme.{u}} (abel : DivSch ⟶ J)
    (hdiv : ∀ y : J, ∃ (_ : Algebra k (J.residueField y))
      (_ : IsIntegral (relCurve C (J.residueField y)))
      (_ : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))
      (_ : QuasiCompact
        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))
      (D : (relCurve C (J.residueField y)).CurveDivisor) (_ : 0 ≤ D),
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg (J.residueField y) D = (g : ℤ))
    (hlift : ∀ y : J, ∃ q : Spec (J.residueField y) ⟶ DivSch,
      q ≫ abel = J.fromSpecResidueField y)
    (fallback : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K], Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ J)
    (hcompat : ∀ y : J, ∀ (D : (relCurve C (J.residueField y)).CurveDivisor)
      (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg (J.residueField y) D = (g : ℤ))
      [IsIntegral (relCurve C (J.residueField y))]
      [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y)))]
      [QuasiCompact
        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y)))]
      [Algebra k (J.residueField y)],
      (effectiveDivisorClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D hD hdeg).left ≫ abel
        = J.fromSpecResidueField y) :
    ∃ pt, IsAbelClassifyCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 abel pt
      ∧ (∀ y : J, ∃ (_ : Algebra k (J.residueField y))
          (_ : IsIntegral (relCurve C (J.residueField y)))
          (_ : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
            (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))
          (_ : QuasiCompact
            (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))
          (D : (relCurve C (J.residueField y)).CurveDivisor) (_ : 0 ≤ D)
          (_ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg (J.residueField y) D = (g : ℤ)),
          pt (J.residueField y) D = J.fromSpecResidueField y) := by
  classical
  refine ⟨fun K _ _ _ _ _ D =>
      if h : 0 ≤ D ∧ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K D = (g : ℤ) then
        (effectiveDivisorClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D h.1 h.2).left ≫ abel
      else fallback K, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro K _ _ _ _ _ D hD hdeg
    show _ = if h : 0 ≤ D ∧ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K D = (g : ℤ) then
          (effectiveDivisorClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D h.1 h.2).left ≫ abel
        else fallback K
    rw [dif_pos ⟨hD, hdeg⟩]
  · intro y
    obtain ⟨_, _, _, _, D, hD, hdeg⟩ := hdiv y
    refine ⟨‹_›, ‹_›, ‹_›, ‹_›, D, hD, hdeg, ?_⟩
    show (if h : 0 ≤ D ∧ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg (J.residueField y) D = (g : ℤ) then
          (effectiveDivisorClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D h.1 h.2).left ≫ abel
        else fallback (J.residueField y)) = _
    rw [dif_pos ⟨hD, hdeg⟩]
    exact hcompat y D hD hdeg

end Probe

end AlgebraicGeometry

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

example : QuasiCompact

example : Algebra k (J.residueField y) := by infer_instance

1	/-

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyFieldSurj
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum
8	
9	/-!
10	# DAT-J step 3 is one compatibility square, not a construction
11	
12	`Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean` reduced DAT-J to two inputs: a
13	`PicRepDatum k k C` and, for every point `y` of the representing object, a lift
14	
15	> `∃ q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g, q ≫ abel = fromSpecResidueField y`.
16	
17	The lift has been read as "the Abel map is surjective on points", i.e. as geometry still
18	to be done. **The morphism half is already built**, in a rooted file, and what is missing
19	is only that it sits over the right point.
20	
21	## What is landed, and had no consumer
22	
23	`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean` (rooted, sorry-free) carries the whole *fibrewise*
24	chain, and the reason it is short is that **over a field the certificate is free**:
25	
26	* `DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_deg` (`:104`) — over a field `K`, an adaptation whose
27	  presentation divisor has degree `n` is `IsCertified n`.  All seven clauses: projectivity
28	  and both flat-cokernel clauses are `Module.Free.of_divisionRing` instances, `(c1)`
29	  finiteness is `moduleFinite_colength`, and the `(c2)` rank clause is the *unconditional*
30	  CRT identity `deg_presentationDivisor` read against the degree hypothesis.  No support
31	  separation is needed — which the file records as a deviation of record, since full
32	  support separation is unachievable when a support point lies in both charts' overlap.
33	* `exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq` (`:147`) — hence every effective degree-`g` divisor over
34	  `K` *is* the divisor of a `DivFam`.
35	* `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` (`:217`) — and it classifies, giving
36	  `overSpec k K ⟶ divSchemeOver …`, characterized by `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec`
37	  (`:231`).
38	
39	This is the sharp form of critical-path §7.6's own observation that the `DivFamZar` no-go
40	is a purely *relative* phenomenon, **vacuous over a field**: the difficulty that makes U2
41	hard does not exist fibrewise.
42	
43	## What is therefore actually missing
44	
45	`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec` says the morphism is `divRepClassifyZar` of a family
46	presenting `D`.  It says **nothing about `abel`**.  So joining it to `hlift` needs exactly
47	one statement — that classifying an effective divisor and then applying the Abel map
48	returns the class of that divisor's point:
49	
50	> `AbelCompatible abel` : for every field point and every effective degree-`g` divisor `D`
51	> over it, `(effectiveDivisorClassifyZar … D …).left ≫ abel` is the morphism `Spec K ⟶ J`
52	> named by the class of `D`.
53	
54	That is a *compatibility square*, not a surjectivity theorem, and it is the recorded
55	"groups agree ≠ maps agree" gap (inbox `I-0525`): a bijection between divisor classes and
56	`DivScheme`-points is unusable until the square relating the two named morphisms lands.
57	
58	## Main declarations
59	
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelClassifyCompatible` — the square, as a named interface.
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible` — the square plus
62	  fibrewise effectivity gives the `hlift` obligation **verbatim** as
63	  `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` / `PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` consume it.
64	
65	## What this does NOT do
66	
67	It produces no `AbelClassifyCompatible` and no effectivity witness, so it builds no
68	`JacobianData`.  It removes the *construction* from DAT-J step 3 and leaves a square and
69	an effectivity input, both stated here rather than assumed anywhere.
70	-/
71	
72	set_option autoImplicit false
73	set_option quotPrecheck false
74	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
75	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
76	
77	universe u
78	
79	open CategoryTheory Limits
80	
81	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
82	
83	open Scheme
84	
85	section AbelSquare
86	
87	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
88	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
89	
90	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftAbelSquare :
91	    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
92	
93	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
94	  [IsIntegral C.left]
95	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
96	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
97	  [IsDominant pi]
98	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
99	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
100	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
101	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
102	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
103	variable (g : ℕ)
104	variable (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
105	variable (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
106	variable (r1 r2 : ℕ)
107	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
108	  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
109	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
110	  ↥(divisorSections k
111	    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
112	
113	local notation "DivSch" =>
114	  DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
115	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
116	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)
117	
118	/-! ## The square -/
119	
120	/-- **The Abel-compatibility square** — the one statement standing between the landed
121	fibrewise classification and DAT-J's `hlift` obligation.
122	
123	At a scheme `J` and a morphism `abel : DivScheme g ⟶ J`, this says: whenever a point `y`
124	of `J` is presented by an effective degree-`g` divisor `D` on the curve over its own
125	residue field — presented in the sense that the classifying morphism composed with `abel`
126	is required to be `fromSpecResidueField y` — the composite is that structural morphism.
127	
128	Stated as a hypothesis over `y` and `D` rather than as a surjectivity claim, because that
129	is the shape `hlift` consumes: `hlift` needs, *for each* `y`, *some* divisor; the geometric
130	content is producing `D`, and the bookkeeping content is this square.  Separating them is
131	the point of this file (compare inbox `I-0525`: an isomorphism of class groups is unusable
132	without the square relating the named morphisms). -/
133	def IsAbelClassifyCompatible {J : Scheme.{u}} (abel : DivSch ⟶ J)
134	    (pt : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
135	      [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
136	      [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))],
137	      (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor → (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ J)) : Prop :=
138	  ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
139	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
140	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
141	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
142	    (D : (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor) (hD : 0 ≤ D)
143	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K D = (g : ℤ)),
144	    (effectiveDivisorClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D hD hdeg).left ≫ abel
145	      = pt K D
146	
147	/-- **The `hlift` obligation from the square plus fibrewise effectivity** — `DAT-J` step 3
148	in the exact shape `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
149	`PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` consume (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean`,
150	`Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean`).
151	
152	The lift is `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` of the supplied divisor, and the triangle is the
153	square.  Note what is *not* here: no surjectivity of the Abel map on points is proved, and
154	no divisor is produced — `heff` is the honest geometric input (Riemann–Roch: a degree-`g`
155	class on a curve of genus `g` over a field has an effective representative, to be spelled
156	with `exists_effective_of_picClass` / `riemann_inequality` and **never** with
157	`riemann_inequality_curve`, which imports `Challenge.lean`). -/
158	theorem exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible {J : Scheme.{u}} (abel : DivSch ⟶ J)
159	    (pt : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
160	      [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
161	      [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))],
162	      (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor → (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ J))
163	    (hsq : IsAbelClassifyCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 abel pt)
164	    (heff : ∀ y : J, ∃ (_ : Algebra k (J.residueField y))
165	      (_ : IsIntegral (relCurve C (J.residueField y)))
166	      (_ : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
167	        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))
168	      (_ : QuasiCompact
169	        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))
170	      (D : (relCurve C (J.residueField y)).CurveDivisor) (_ : 0 ≤ D)
171	      (_ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg (J.residueField y) D = (g : ℤ)),
172	      pt (J.residueField y) D = J.fromSpecResidueField y) :
173	    ∀ y : J, ∃ q : Spec (J.residueField y) ⟶ DivSch,
174	      q ≫ abel = J.fromSpecResidueField y := by
175	  intro y
176	  obtain ⟨_, _, _, _, D, hD, hdeg, hpt⟩ := heff y
177	  exact ⟨(effectiveDivisorClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D hD hdeg).left,
178	    (hsq (J.residueField y) D hD hdeg).trans hpt⟩
179	
180	end AbelSquare
181	
182	end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianDataAbelSquare

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
universe u
open CategoryTheory Limits
namespace AlgebraicGeometry
open Scheme

section EffProbe

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]

-- Q1: do the two Module.Finite instances synthesise at the `relCurve` alias?
example : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C K).moduleKSheaf K) 0) := by
  infer_instance

example : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C K).moduleKSheaf K) 1) := by
  infer_instance

-- Q2: IsIntegral / Smooth / QuasiCompact at the alias (heff bundles these as DATA;
-- if they are instances the bundling is redundant).
example : IsIntegral (relCurve C K) := by infer_instance
example : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
    (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := by infer_instance
example : QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := by infer_instance

end EffProbe

section KappaProbe

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (y : J.left)

-- Q3: is `Algebra k (J.left.residueField y)` available for an Over (Spec k) object?
example : Algebra k (J.left.residueField y) := by infer_instance

end KappaProbe

/-! Q4: the degree arithmetic of `heff` from `exists_effective_of_picClass`:
given a class of degree exactly `g` and `chi = 1 - g`, is `1 ≤ deg + chi` automatic,
and does the returned `E` have degree `g`? -/
section DegProbe

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

theorem probe_deg_g_effective (g : ℕ)
    (hchi : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    (W : X.CurveDivisor) (hW : CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ)) :
    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K E = (g : ℤ) ∧
      CurveDivisor.picClass K E = CurveDivisor.picClass K W := by
  obtain ⟨E, hE0, hEc⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass W (by rw [hW, hchi]; omega)
  refine ⟨E, hE0, ?_, hEc⟩
  have h := congrArg (classDeg K) hEc
  rw [classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass] at h
  rw [h, hW]

end DegProbe

end AlgebraicGeometry
